title.en: What Does It Mean to Learn?

summary.en: Use cat pictures and fruit cards to discover what learning from examples means.
summary.bn: বিড়ালের ছবি আর ফলের কার্ড দিয়ে বোঝো, উদাহরণ দেখে শেখা মানে কী।

keywords: What Does It Mean to Learn?

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: A picture wall, not a perfect definition
Two routes to a fruit-sorting rule
Teach a classmate an unfamiliar category

practice.title: A counterexample cat
practice.statementHtml: Describe a dog picture that defeats the pointed-ear rule. Explain what the rule missed.
practice.answerHtml: A small dog with pointed ears defeats it. Both cats and dogs can share that clue, so ears alone do not identify the category.

practice.title: Rule source
practice.statementHtml: Compare Nana dictating a dividing size with Tuktuk choosing one from named cards.
hints: Ask who selected the dividing point.
practice.answerHtml: In the first case Nana chose the rule. In the second, people wrote a comparison procedure and the examples helped select the rule. Only that second selection learns from the supplied cards.

practice.title: Reuse tomorrow
practice.statementHtml: A saved size-five rule sees a size-six fruit with its name hidden. Describe prediction and checking as two steps.
practice.answerHtml: The rule predicts mango because six lies beyond five. Afterwards uncover the actual name to check. The prediction step alone does not change the rule.

practice.title: Wrong teaching card
practice.statementHtml: One of six animal cards has the wrong name. Explain how this can hurt learning and suggest a remedy.
hints: Consider where the learner gets its evidence.
practice.answerHtml: The learner may adjust toward a false relationship. Check the card against a reliable source, correct the name, then train and assess again on different examples. Blaming the learner does not repair misleading evidence.

quiz.prompt: In the animal cards, why is “pointed ears means cat” an unreliable rule?
options: Every cat has floppy ears
Card F is a dog with pointed ears
The card names change ear shapes
Only white animals can be cats
quiz.explanation: Read A and F together: both mention pointed ears but their answers differ. One clue cannot settle this collection.

caption.en: Six named animal cards; pointed ears occur in both kinds.
caption.bn: ছয় প্রাণীর নামসহ কার্ড; দুই দলেই খাড়া কান আছে।

quiz.prompt: Read the fruit dots. Which new size-seven fruit would the size-five dividing rule predict?
options: Apple, because sweetness is unknown
It must copy the nearest card number
Mango, because seven is to the right of five
A guaranteed real mango in every case
quiz.explanation: The saved rule uses size, so seven goes to the mango side. That is a prediction; the real name still needs checking.

caption.en: Predict Apple on or left of size 5; Mango on the right.
caption.bn: আকার 5 বা বাঁয়ে আপেল, ডানে আম অনুমান।

quiz.prompt: Mina recognises an unfamiliar striped cat after seeing several cats. What best shows learning?
options: She repeats only the names in their original order
She reads a fixed bell schedule
She needs a perfect written definition before any guess
She uses earlier examples on a new case
quiz.explanation: The unfamiliar animal tests whether earlier experience helps. Repeating the old sequence would only show memory.

quiz.prompt: Nana supplies the exact size-five instruction himself. What has Tuktuk done by obeying it?
options: Followed a human-written rule
Chosen that rule by comparing example answers
Proved that all fruit names follow size
Acquired human feelings about mangoes
quiz.explanation: Nana selected the cutoff. To call its selection learning, examples must help choose or adjust the rule.

quiz.prompt: What role does a model play after training has ended?
options: It is the original basket of physical fruit
It stores a pattern that can be used for new predictions
It must ask a human for every old answer again
It guarantees correct answers outside its experience
quiz.explanation: A model is reusable. Reuse is useful even though unfamiliar cases can expose errors.

quiz.prompt: Tuktuk changes its fence after comparing predictions with known names. What was learned from examples?
options: How to feel hungry
The measurement units without being told
Which tried fence to keep
Every possible fruit name in the world
quiz.explanation: The comparison procedure was programmed by people. The known names helped it select a fence.

quiz.prompt: A new apple is size seven, but the saved rule predicts mango. What follows?
options: The true apple must become a mango
Training never happened
The old cards were all necessarily wrong
The learned rule can still make a mistake
quiz.explanation: Learning and error can coexist. A successful old count did not cover every later case.

quiz.prompt: Which description of machine learning fits our card activity?
options: Using examples to build a reusable prediction model
Any action performed without a human pressing a button
A computer feeling curiosity like Mina
A promise that the largest pile always produces truth
quiz.explanation: The examples influence the reusable rule. Automatic action alone does not show that kind of learning.

quiz.prompt: Why include cats with different colours and tails?
options: Only identical pictures can teach a category
Variety helps show which differences should not change the name
The colour of the paper must determine the name
Different pictures make labels unnecessary
quiz.explanation: A learner seeing only one look may follow an accidental clue. Varied, correctly named examples offer better evidence.

quiz.prompt: When the same saved rule names tomorrow’s fruit, must it be training again?
options: Yes; every prediction replaces every learned rule
Yes; a model disappears after one prediction
No; using a model can happen without changing it
No; because a model cannot ever be updated
quiz.explanation: Applying a fixed model is different from adjusting one. It can later be updated through another learning process.

keyPoints.en: Examples give a learner cases to practise on.
A person may write a rule directly.
Learning can select a rule by comparing guesses with known answers.
keyPoints.bn: জানা উত্তরের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে শেখার নিয়ম বাছা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A model stores a pattern that can be reused.
keyPoints.bn: Model রেখে দিলে পরে আবার ব্যবহার করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A fresh case can reveal a mistake that old cards missed.
keyPoints.bn: নতুন কার্ডে আগের অদেখা ভুল ধরা পড়তে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Computers can learn patterns without having a human mind.
keyPoints.bn: ধরন শেখার জন্য মানুষের মন থাকা জরুরি নয়।

examQuestions.question: Explain machine learning and a model using the fruit-card story.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Machine learning uses examples to build a model for new predictions. Tuktuk compares fence positions against known fruit names and keeps a useful rule. The saved fence is its model; a later guess may still be wrong.

examQuestions.question: Six cards are apples at sizes 2, 3, 4 and mangoes at sizes 6, 7, 8. Predict apple through size 3 and mango above it. Count mistakes.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The size-4 apple is called mango. The other two apples and all three mangoes match. There is exactly one mistake among six cards.

examQuestions.question: Design a paper test that distinguishes remembered card order from useful animal recognition.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Show four named animal pictures, then introduce two unfamiliar drawings in a different order. Record guesses before revealing names. A learner relying only on the old sequence fails when order changes; correct new guesses offer limited evidence of a reusable pattern.

examQuestions.question: Why does a correct guess not establish human-like understanding?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A programmed process can find relationships and select a name without feelings or a human account of the animal. Describe the observed prediction skill rather than inferring a mind. Check unfamiliar examples and state the limits of the task.
